# Prefer the highest non-excluded replacement even when the proxy has a
# newer version of the module.
go mod tidy
grep '^require example.com/deprecated/b v1.0.0$' go.mod
go build ./...
go mod tidy -diff

# When only the excluded replacement remains, use the proxy instead.
go mod edit -droprequire=example.com/deprecated/b -dropreplace=example.com/deprecated/b@v1.0.0
go mod tidy
grep '^require example.com/deprecated/b v1.9.0$' go.mod
go build ./...
go mod tidy -diff

# With no tagged releases, @latest falls back to pseudo-versions.
env GOPROXY=off
go mod edit -replace=example.com/local@v0.0.0-20220101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa=./local -replace=example.com/local@v0.0.0-20230101000000-bbbbbbbbbbbb=./local -exclude=example.com/local@v0.0.0-20230101000000-bbbbbbbbbbbb
go list -m example.com/local@latest
stdout '^example.com/local v0.0.0-20220101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa$'

-- local/go.mod --
module example.com/local
-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27

replace (
	example.com/deprecated/b v1.0.0 => ./fork
	example.com/deprecated/b v1.1.0 => ./fork
)
exclude example.com/deprecated/b v1.1.0
-- app.go --
package app
import _ "example.com/deprecated/b"
-- fork/go.mod --
module example.com/deprecated/b

go 1.27
-- fork/b.go --
package b
